hero.tag: Senior Software Engineer · Full-Stack · AI · Data Engineering · R&D
hero.subtitle: Software engineer and PhD in mechanics, I build applications that turn data into practical tools. From modelling through to production, every solution is designed to be reliable, durable and to meet the real needs of the people who rely on it day to day.

about.p1: I’ve designed and shipped applications in both France and the United Kingdom, within teams that differed widely in their working methods, their industries and their cultures. Those experiences taught me that no two projects are alike. Before proposing a solution, taking the time to understand the context, the goals and the constraints has become second nature.
about.p2: To me, the value of software isn’t measured by its technical complexity but by its usefulness. Good software is, above all, a tool that simplifies work, saves time and meets its users’ needs for the long term.
about.p3: That conviction runs through every technical choice I make. I favour solutions that are simple, robust and built to evolve — designed to be understood, maintained and extended by a whole team, without depending on whoever first designed them. An architecture doesn’t need to be spectacular to succeed: it succeeds when it stays reliable, readable and useful, even years after it goes into production.

research.meta_desc: Peer-reviewed scientific publications: mechanics, wave propagation and numerical modelling applied to underground structures.
research.lead: Before I designed software, I did research.
research.intro_1: My doctorate addressed an engineering challenge: understanding and predicting how underground structures — tunnels, cavities — respond when subjected to mechanical and seismic waves. A subject at the heart of how such infrastructure is designed, made reliable and kept safe.
research.intro_2: This work led me to cross several disciplines: continuum mechanics, wave propagation, mathematical modelling and numerical methods. But above all it taught me a method: break a complex problem down, build a reliable model, solve it rigorously, then test the results against reality. An approach I bring to every software engineering project today.
research.impact_lead: Research was not a detour in my career: it is the foundation of how I work.
research.impact_1_d: Break down an ill-posed problem, frame it, then solve it methodically.
research.impact_2_d: Turn a real problem into a workable model without losing the underlying physics.
research.impact_3_d: Think in terms of cost, accuracy and convergence before writing a single line.
research.impact_4_d: Explicit assumptions, reproducible results, verifiable conclusions.
research.impact_5_d: Work with large volumes of data and extract the signal that matters.
research.impact_6_d: Systematically test the model against measurements, and distrust both.
research.impact_7_d: Make a complex idea clear to a non-specialist audience.
research.impact_8_d: Sustain demanding, self-directed work over several years and see it through.
